extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations; environmental compliance officers; facility engineers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory compliance requirements for design, equipment, monitoring, testing, leak detection, and recordkeeping at bulk gasoline terminals and pipeline breakout stations subject to the cited subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design-capacity based applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must equip, maintain, and operate each gasoline storage vessel with a design capacity greater than or equal to 75 m3 according to the requirements in §60.112b(a)(1) through (4) of this chapter, except certain subsections; alternatively you may elect to comply with subpart WW as specified in §60.110b(e)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original text references the option to follow §60.112b or subpart WW; applicability hinges on vessel design capacity ≥75 m3. Follow cited cross-references for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal floating roof LEL limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip, maintain, and operate each internal floating roof control system to maintain vapor concentration within the storage vessel above the floating roof at or below 25 percent of the lower explosive limit (LEL) on a 5-minute rolling average basis without the use of purge gas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance determined using methods in §63.425(j). A deviation of the LEL level is an inspection failure under §60.113b(a)(2) or §63.1063(d)(2) and must be remedied per the listed timeframes; repairs must be confirmed via re-monitoring to meet the LEL within required timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: External floating roof fitting controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip, maintain, and operate each gasoline external floating roof storage vessel (design capacity ≥75 m3) with fitting controls as specified in §60.112b(a)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fitting control specifics are in the cited provision. If applicable, fitting controls required in paragraph (b)(3) must be installed the next time the vessel is completely emptied and degassed, or by May 8, 2034, whichever is first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates by facility construction date
rubrics_metrics.description: Each gasoline storage vessel must comply 'as expeditiously as practicable' but no later than specific dates depending on when the facility commenced construction (before Feb 8, 1994; after Feb 8, 1994 and on or before June 10, 2022; after June 10, 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deadlines include Dec 15, 1997 (historical), May 8, 2027 transitions, and for new construction compliance upon startup or July 8, 2024, whichever is later. Consult paragraph (c)(1)-(3) for exact applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: LDAR program implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator shall implement a leak detection and repair (LDAR) program for all equipment in gasoline service according to paragraph (b) or (c) as applicable and minimize gasoline vapor losses per paragraph (d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LDAR program choices and minimization measures are elaborated in subsequent paragraphs. Applicability determined by paragraph (e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly leak inspections with sensory methods allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a monthly leak inspection of all equipment in gasoline service. Detection methods incorporating sight, sound, and smell are acceptable. Each piece of equipment shall be inspected during the loading of a gasoline cargo tank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a logbook signed by owner/operator at completion. Each detection must be recorded and repaired per timelines (initial attempt within 5 calendar days; repair or replacement within 15 calendar days) unless delay justified to Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: LDAR logbook contents and signing
rubrics_metrics.description: A logbook shall be used and shall be signed by the owner or operator at the completion of each inspection. A section of the log shall contain a list, summary description, or diagram(s) showing the location of all equipment in gasoline service at the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each detection of a liquid or vapor leak shall be recorded. Logs support required repair timelines and documentation for Administrator review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak repair timelines and delay justification
rubrics_metrics.description: When a leak is detected, an initial attempt at repair shall be made as soon as practicable, but no later than 5 calendar days after detection. Repair or replacement shall be completed within 15 calendar days after detection, except delay allowed upon demonstration to the Administrator that repair within 15 days is not feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delay demonstration must provide reasons and expected completion date. Repairs must be confirmed effective as required elsewhere (e.g., re-monitoring).

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument alternative to sensory LDAR
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to compliance with monthly sensory inspections and associated provisions, owners/operators may implement an instrument leak monitoring program that has been demonstrated to the Administrator as at least equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalency must be demonstrated to the Administrator; maintain documentation of equivalence and operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced LDAR monitoring frequencies when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Comply with §60.502a(j) except as provided: OGI monitoring frequency shall be semiannually rather than quarterly; Method 21 monitoring of pumps/valves shall be semiannually rather than quarterly; monitoring of pressure relief devices shall be semiannually and within 5 days after pressure release rather than quarterly and within 5 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These frequency relaxations apply per paragraph (c)(1)-(3) for affected facilities; verify exact cross-references for instrument-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization measures for extended vapor releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators shall not handle gasoline in a manner that would result in vapor releases for extended periods. Measures include: minimize gasoline spills; clean up spills expeditiously; cover all open gasoline containers with gasketed seal when not in use; minimize gasoline sent to open waste collection systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List is illustrative ('include, but are not limited to'); facilities should implement practical procedures to address these items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance testing under representative conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance tests shall be conducted under representative conditions when liquid product is being loaded into gasoline cargo tanks and include periods between cargo tank loading provided that liquid product loading occurs for at least a portion of each 5-minute block of the performance test. Tests may not be conducted during malfunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record process information necessary to document operating conditions during the test with explanation that conditions represent normal operation. Make records available to Administrator upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gasoline loading rack vapor system performance test methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a performance test on vapor processing and collection systems using either (i) test methods/procedures in §60.503 (with 500 ppm leak reading for repairs) or (ii) alternative test methods under §63.7(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using flares meeting §63.11(b), certain §60.503(c) requirements do not apply; demonstrate compliance per §63.11(b) and §60.503(a),(b),(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish monitored operating parameter value
rubrics_metrics.description: During performance tests, determine a monitored operating parameter value for the vapor processing system by (i) continuously recording the operating parameter under §63.427(a); (ii) determining a value based on parameter data supplemented by engineering assessments and manufacturer's recommendations; and (iii) providing Administrator approval rationale including data, calculations, monitoring frequency, averaging time, and explanation that demonstrates continuous compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For subsequent tests, document reasons for any change in the operating parameter value since previous performance test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loading rack CEMS initial and subsequent testing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: For sources subject to §63.422(b)(2), conduct the first performance test/evaluation of CEMS within 180 days of beginning compliance; a previous performance test may satisfy requirement if specific conditions (conducted on/after May 8, 2022; no process/control changes; methods/time/requirements conform; combustion zone temperature recorded; test demonstrates compliance) are met. Subsequent tests: 60 calendar months for mass loading limit systems; 12 months for concentration-limit CEMS evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow paragraph (c)(2)-(4) criteria for reuse of earlier tests and test periodicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gasoline storage vessel compliance with §60.113b
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of gasoline storage vessels subject to §63.423 must comply with §60.113b and, if applicable, additional provisions in §63.425(j). If a closed vent system and control device are used (per §60.112b(a)(3)), owners/operators must also comply with additional paragraph (d)(1) or (d)(2) requirements as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (d)(2) specifies alternate compliance where flare is used and replaces certain §60.502a text. Verify exact cross-references for device-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 27 pressure/vacuum test parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct Method 27 pressure and vacuum tests using a time period of 5 minutes. Initial pressure Pi = 460 mm H2O (18 in. H2O) gauge. Initial vacuum Vi = 150 mm H2O (6 in. H2O) gauge. Implement paragraph (e)(1)(i) or (ii) maxima per table 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance dates differ by construction date; table 1 lists allowable pressure/vacuum changes by cargo tank capacity (see table for exact numeric limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection test instrument standard (Method 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Leak detection test shall be performed using Method 21. A vapor-tight gasoline cargo tank shall have no leaks at any time when tested per these procedures. The instrument reading that defines a leak is 10,000 ppm (as propane). Use propane to calibrate instrument setting span at the leak definition. Detector response to 90% must be <8 seconds with probe attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Method 21 procedures exactly; instrument calibration and performance requirements specified to ensure validity of leak/no-leak determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous performance pressure decay test (Method 27) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous performance pressure decay test shall be performed using Method 27, conducting only the positive pressure test with a 5-minute time period and initial pressure Pi of 460 mm H2O; the maximum allowable 5-minute pressure change must meet the values in the fourth column of table 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the continuous performance standard; apply appropriate table values for tank capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL monitoring frequency and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: LEL monitoring for internal floating roof storage vessels at §63.423(b)(2) must be conducted at least once every 12 months and at other times upon Administrator request. If measurement cannot be performed due to high wind (per paragraph j(3)(iii)), perform within 30 days of previous attempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If tubing used, it must be non-crimping Teflon or inert material; calibration checks and measurement conditions specified in following paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL meter calibration before/after measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Calibration of the LEL meter must be checked per manufacturer specifications immediately before and after measurements. If tubing is used, attach tubing during calibration so calibration gas travels through whole system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If span or offset checks fail, recalibrate/replace meter and repeat measurements as required; details for span check and offset given in (j)(2)(i)-(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL span check specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Span check: use calibration gas recommended by LEL meter manufacturer containing a single hydrocarbon at concentration corresponding to 50% LEL (e.g., 2.50% vol methane). Vendor must provide Certificate of Analysis; certified concentration within ±2%. LEL span response must be between 49% and 51%. If not met, recalibrate/replace and repeat as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Span check must be done immediately before and after measurements; repeated measurements required if post-measurement span fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrumental offset (zero) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Check instrumental offset using certified zero air or ambient free of organics. Pre-measurement instrumental offset response must be 0% LEL. If not met, recalibrate/replace meter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offset check fails after measurements, recalibrate/replace and repeat measurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL measurement location, duration, logging frequency
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurements must be collected no more than 3 feet above the internal floating roof. Measurements shall be taken for a minimum of 20 minutes, logging at least once every 15 seconds, or until one 5-minute average exceeds the allowed level. Measurements should be conducted when roof is floating with limited product movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wind speed conditions apply: conduct when wind speed at top of tank ≤5 mph to the extent practicable, and never when sustained wind at top of tank > (annual average wind speed or 15 mph, whichever is less).

rubrics_metrics.name: LEL correction factors and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine actual vapor concentration, multiply percent LEL 'as the calibration gas' by published gasoline vapor correction factor for meter/cal gas; if none, use published correction factor for butane as surrogate corresponding to calibration gas. Then calculate one-minute averages from corrected measurements and compute 5-minute rolling averages; each 5-minute rolling average must meet the LEL level in §63.423(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-minute average: arithmetic average of corrected individual measurements taken at least once every 15 seconds during the minute. Five-minute rolling average: arithmetic average of previous five one-minute readings starting with end of fifth minute; compute new five-minute average each minute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous monitoring system (CMS) installation and maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators subject to §63.422(b)(1) shall install, calibrate, certify, operate, and maintain a CMS according to manufacturer's specifications as specified in paragraph (a)(1)-(4), except as allowed in (a)(5). For thermal oxidation systems, a CPMS capable of measuring temperature must be installed in the firebox or in ductwork immediately downstream before substantial heat exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS/CPMS specifics follow §63.427(a)-(c). Alternative monitoring methods may be allowed as specified (e.g., §60.504a(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate vapor processing within established operating parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Operate vapor processing system so as not to exceed the operating parameter value(s) (or not go below for specified parameters) established per §63.425(b); operation outside the operating parameter value constitutes a violation/deviation for the applicable emission standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an alternative parameter is approved, operate consistent with that alternative parameter value. Exceedance or going below is a violation under §63.422(b)(1) or deviation under §63.422(b)(2) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring record retention and cross-reference compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Gasoline storage vessels subject to §63.423 must comply with monitoring requirements in §60.116b, except records shall be kept for at least 5 years. If closed vent and control device used, also comply with additional paragraph (e)(1) or (2) monitoring requirements (which reference §63.427(a) or §60.504a(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain records for at least 5 years; follow device-specific cross-referenced monitoring rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial notifications and recordkeeping retention general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial notifications required under §63.9(b)(2) must be submitted by 1 year after source becomes subject or by Dec 16, 1996, whichever later. Owners/operators must keep records of test results for each gasoline cargo tank loading for at least 5 years; other recordkeeping requirements similarly specify 5-year retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation file must include specific items for each test (name, cargo tank owner/address, ID, location/date, tester, inspector, repairs, test results) per paragraph (b)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of vapor tightness testing and deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep records of annual certification testing and continuous performance testing and a documentation file up-to-date for each gasoline cargo tank loading including specific items (see paragraph (b)(3)(i)-(viii)). Also keep records when loading occurs without proper vapor tightness documentation or cargo tanks not using submerged filling, incompatible equipment, or improperly connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of missing documentation must include cargo tank owner/address, ID, date/time loaded without documentation, and date proper documentation received or statement it was never received. Records of improperly connected or not submerged filling events must include date/time, type of deviation, cargo tank ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous monitoring data reporting for §63.422(b)(1) sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep an up-to-date, readily accessible record of continuous monitoring data required under §63.427(a) indicating time intervals when gasoline cargo tank loadings occurred (or record operating parameter data only during such loadings). Record and report with notification of compliance status all data, calculations, engineering assessments, and manufacturer's recommendations used to determine operating parameter value under §63.425(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a flare under §63.11(b) to comply, also report flare design (steam/air/non-assisted) and all visible emissions readings, heat content, flow rate, and exit velocity determinations made during compliance determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written procedures and performance evaluation plan retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep written procedures required under §63.8(d)(2) on record for life of affected source or until no longer subject; keep superseded versions of performance evaluation plan on record for 5 years after each revision; include program of corrective action in plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make procedures and plans available for inspection by Administrator upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal oxidation/CPMS/TOC CEMS recordkeeping and deviation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For thermal oxidation systems, pressure CPMS, and vapor recovery systems used to comply with §63.422(b)(2), maintain records of applicable operating/emission limits, each 3-hour rolling average combustion zone temperature, each 5-minute average pressure CPMS reading, each 3-hour rolling average TOC (as propane) measured by TOC CEMS, and for each deviation record start/date/time, duration, cause, and corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also record CMS outages/out-of-control events (start/date/time, duration, cause, corrective action), inspections/calibrations with unique identifier/make/model/date, and details for TOC CEMS outages and alternative vapor recovery limited alternative usage (see paragraph (d)(1)(vi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare and visible emissions monitoring records
rubrics_metrics.description: For each flare used to comply with §63.422(b)(2) and thermal oxidation systems using flare monitoring alternative, maintain monitoring device outputs for pilot flame presence per §63.670(b) for minimum 2 years and retain records of 15-minute blocks during which there was at least one minute no pilot flame when vapors were routed to flare for minimum 5 years. Maintain visible emissions observation records per Method 22 for minimum 3 years with specified details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visible emissions: include date, start/end time, and number of minutes with visible emissions. For partial observations, include estimates of cumulative minutes in 2-hour period when full 2-hour Method 22 not conducted. Also record 15-minute block periods when operating values outside limits with identification of specific limit not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15-minute block averaging and flow record retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain 15-minute block average cumulative flows for thermal oxidation/flare vent gas and, if applicable, total steam, perimeter assist air, premix assist air monitored under §63.670(i), with date and start/end time. If multiple monitoring locations used, retain 15-minute block average flows for each location for minimum 2 years and the cumulative flows used in calculations for minimum 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These records feed compliance demonstrations and must be retained as specified (2 or 5 years) depending on use.
